resources.string: Log your periods and insights about your cycle will appear here.
Your first cycle is in progress
Insights appear once you log the start of your next period.
The shaded band is 24 to 38 days, the typical range. Tap a bar for details.
Cycle starting %1$s: %2$s, not used for predictions
These are patterns in what you logged, not a diagnosis. Cadence isn\'t a medical device. The ranges come from the International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO).
Your recent cycles have averaged %1$s. Cycles shorter than 24 days are less common and can be worth mentioning to a clinician.
Your recent cycles have averaged %1$s. Cycles longer than 38 days are less common and can be worth mentioning to a clinician.
Your shortest and longest recent cycles differ by %1$s. A difference of more than 7 to 9 days is worth mentioning to a clinician.
Your period starting %1$s lasted %2$s. Bleeding for more than 8 days is worth mentioning to a clinician.
It\'s been %1$s since your last logged period. If you haven\'t just missed logging one, this is worth mentioning to a clinician. A pregnancy test can rule out pregnancy.

You logged pain of 7 or more out of 10 on several days in %1$s of your recent periods. Period pain that gets in the way of daily life is worth mentioning to a clinician; there are effective treatments.
Turn off a cycle that wasn\'t typical for you, for example during illness or travel, so it doesn\'t skew predictions.
Log symptoms, moods or tags across three or more cycles and any patterns will show up here.
Things you tend to log at the same point in your cycle. They\'re observations from your own logs, not a diagnosis.
